item.text: The fault is localized: moving a note to Trash overwrites its original `updatedAt`, and restoring overwrites it again. With equal edit times, the restore-all loop then preserves Trash’s reverse-deletion order instead of the original stable list order. I’m checking nearby store conventions and test infrastructure before making the smallest state-layer correction.

item.text: I’ll preserve `updatedAt` during soft-delete and restore, and remove `trashedAt` when restoring instead of replacing the edit timestamp. This keeps the store’s existing array order as the stable tie-breaker while Trash can still sort independently by deletion time. I’m adding a regression test that recreates Lilac → Cobalt → Amber deletion and verifies Amber → Lilac → Cobalt after restore-all.
